# Chapter Six: Life on the Farm

> *"The faithful farmer in spring, reaps a plentiful bounty in autumn."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

Marcus awoke before the sun, as the remnants of the same dream that had continued to plague him since returning to earth still held fresh in his mind, the woman still appeared, the same high born dress and golden hair as the two of them stood stalwart upon the grey cliffs eyes leveled to the horizon, watching as the water rose and fell, the thrumming of the baritone beat resonating over the rocks drowning out even the crashing of the waves upon the granite jetty far below. Over the past few months the dreams had persisted when waking, making them seem more like memories then actual dreams.

Who is this woman? he wondered; her face still fresh in his mind. Closing his eyes, he summoned the vision of her, every inch of it committed to memory.

There was something about her, not attraction he pondered, but more like danger, something about her screamed danger, but he didn’t know if it meant danger for him or for the hidden threat that loomed.

After a few moments he opened his eyes.

trying to will the picture of her away,

back to the deep recesses of his mind until the next time the dream emerged, but still the vision of her lingered.

The way she looked at him sent a shiver down his spine as if somehow he was the answer to an important question or a solution to a problem, the way a mechanic might look at a prized tool he mused, pushing the scene from his mind he instead focused on the simple room surrounding him, the old wooden planked walls of the barn’s second floor were worn but sturdy and despite the gouged wood and scratched paint it was clean enough to eat off of he thought with a swell of pride.

He had spent many hours cleaning and making the space his own and now it felt like home, felt safe, sunlight filtered through the small gaps in the building’s seams caused by the decades of settling.

Every day for the past month the morning call of birds had become his alarm clock, the musical sound calming him, smiling at the songs he turned his face towards the small window and closed his eyes again, this time allowing the morning sun to play across his face and warm his cold cheeks.

The rustic wooden barn had become colder, over the past few months, fall moving into the beginnings of winter, now it was cold enough to freeze standing water.

There wasn’t much left for a winter harvest just the cauliflower and kale he mused, “Harvest is here,” he said, loudly to the empty room.

The echoes of his voice played over the dusty rafters causing a sleeping owl to stir and protest with an ethereal hoot, it was a time where the farm would reap the final rewards of the exhausting preparation, all the hard work that had gone into the spring planting, fall harvesting and now the coming winter harvest would now be collected, processed and then brought to market.

Laying in the thick wool blanket, he felt the mild pain as cold air bit into his cheeks causing him to settle deeper into the old heavy green blanket, he lay there enjoying the residual warmth still lingering in the bed with him.

Snaking one arm out of the cocoon of wool he reached down and picked up the igniter, an object that looked akin to large tweezers he had thought the first time Orah had shown him one, each of the two points held a small crystal fastened with metal twine. Stretching his arm as far as it could go, he pushed the igniter into the port of the belly stove that he had rescued and put to use from the pile of junk that sat in the barn below, it wasn’t as nice or new as the crystal heating stoves he had seen in town, but it did the job and the simple wood belly stove comforted him, allowing him to forget the drastic differences between his world and this one.

Bringing the two crystals together he watched as they began to glow putting it to the kindling in the stove it quickly caught fire.

He watched as the small flame began to grow and after a time, he began wriggling more of his body out of the blanket as he tried to balance the warming air with the discomfort of his cold limbs.

As the flames rose from the wood and warmed the small loft he laid back and looked around his domain, the loft area wasn’t grand, but it was clean, and he had spent the last few months making it livable with a bed, stove and shelf on which sat the very few possessions he had in his pockets upon arriving at Orah’s farm.

Feeling a shiver, he wrapped himself back up in the blanket, only his arm exposed as he continued to toss more wood into the small stove, waiting patiently until the room warmed a little more.

Reaching under the pile of cloth he used as a pillow he pulled a worn book out from beneath it. The cover had been made of leather and sported a few carved symbols, the words ‘Making thought reality’ emblazoned with faded gold filigree across the cover.

It was an auspicious title for a book on the basics of magic theory. During one of his trips to the small-town Marcus had stopped into the crystal shop, something he did rarely as the proprietor had more than once tried to engage him in a conversation on magic, trying to bait Marcus into revealing himself a mage,

During one of these trips the owner had shoved the book into his hands, telling him to read it and return it when he was done. Marcus had tried to beg off, tried to return the book but the man simply had shaken his head and refused to take it back.

So, it had sat on his shelf for nearly a week until his curiosity had gotten the best of him. He knew he was a mage, Afterall he had heard the sound of the machine meant to attract new mages.

He was also able to feel the presence of the crystals and the power that flowed through them.

Marcus had begun to read, every night studying the theory and use of Magic, smiling he shook his head.

The thought of magic being real, being something, this world believed in as easily as one did a car or a computer. He himself would not have thought it possible, except for his own experience and the day he watched as the shop owner had lifted a stack of boards within nothing more than his mind.

Marcus had stood there thunderstruck, not knowing what to think or do as the boards floated up to the roof of the small shop where the waiting laborer stood there to install them, until that moment he had been in denial about his own abilities, about who he was, but that had changed that day.

Since then, every night he spent reading more and more about magic and its uses. It wasn’t until three weeks after that, that Marcus had begun working with the exercises in the book.

It took work and concentration, he had spent many nights barely able to lift a small pebble, but the more he practiced the better he got. Using the techniques that the book taught he began to get a sense of his own power, reaching out and feeling items without actually touching them, infusing his will into that touch and moving the objects, the ability was intoxicating.

. In the dead of the night while Orah and the animals all slept, Marcus practiced, taking the lessons to heart and learning about what he was able to do.

As the air of the loft began to heat, he slid the book back under the pillow, once again hiding it from the world as he prepared himself for the day ahead.

Abandoning the blanket and makeshift straw bed, he quickly dressed, taking a final look around to ensure his space was neat before leaving the loft and the barn.

Following the same routine, he did every morning taking comfort in the simple tasks, he went about his chores, Surveying the farm he watched as the morning mist ascended up from the ground lending to it an almost supernatural feel to the farm.

He could hear the bleating and grunts of the various animals as they called for their breakfast and smiled, it was a simple life, but one he had grown to love.

Orah would already be up and cooking breakfast he thought, As he made his way to the stables where he busied himself with putting new hay down for the horses and ensuring their food and water was full before brushing them out gently as they consumed breakfast, continuing his routine he fed the pigs and the goats, ensuring everyone was set for the morning.

After making his rounds he grabbed an arm full of cordwood from the seasoned pile and made his way to the house, with a light knock he entered to the sound of utensils scraping pans and the aroma of onions and cooking meat permeating the small foyer.

Since moving in with Orah in the sense that they lived on the same farm.

Marcus had become quite proficient at taking care of the day-to-day chores that kept the farm running, putting the wood by the hearth he stood back and admired the vision of beauty, Orah oblivious to his pining stare as she busied herself in the kitchen.

Thinking back to those early days he thought about her lessons as he was learning how to operate the farm, he had been clueless Marcus recalled smiling at the thought, remembering the time she had attempted to show him how to use a scythe, he still winced at the mental image.

However, this recent harvest had seen Orah doing most of the work as he followed behind, mimicking her movements and paying rapt attention to the words of wisdom she would convey as they worked.

Today would mark the final winter harvest, once that was complete he would spend his time cutting wood and making repairs as they waited until spring, every task lending to their ability to exist, because, for the first time his life was simply about survival and there was pleasure and pride in that.

In his old world that of computers and cell phones and microwave dinners brought problems and issues that now seemed silly and trivial, there was comfort in stripping down one’s life pitting himself against nature in order to simply carve out an existence.

He was new, inexperienced but in the past few months he had come a long way from the man he had been, a newfound confidence springing from his learned ability to survive.

Marcus still a lot to learn, but Orah was an excellent teacher, she was firm but gentle with her words, ensuring to repeat even the simplest procedures as they moved through the day.

Reflecting on her kindness, he stared at the woman who had become his world, even if he wasn’t ready to admit it.

Marcus had soon come to realize there was never a shortage of work to do on a farm, but he had never been happier in his entire life then he was now, to live one day to the next, pitting himself against the will of mother nature herself.

For the first time Marcus felt he was earning the right to live, the right to survive and that was exhilarating, leaving him with a sense of pride and accomplishment.

Looking around the small building that had come to mean so much to him, representing hearth and home, if he were optimistic, this morning, would also represent his future he thought watching the vision of beauty, over the past few months he had come to realize that this woman was his life, she was unlike anyone he had ever met. This simple farm girl had more intelligence and courage than even the stoutest soldier and a heart that would make Mother Teresa herself seem cold and distant. As he stared longingly at the simple farm girl he had the realization that his life had hope and meaning for the first time, he felt like he was staring at his future, his happiness and his life represented in the delicate smile, intelligent mind and bright eyes of this amazing woman.

Stepping to the left he gently kicked the dirt off his leather boots gaining her attention, Orah looked up with a start and smiled as Marcus continued to ensure he had removed the detritus from the farm work, the smell of the cooking meat and the sounds of her angelic voice as she hummed the now-familiar tune that was common while she worked was almost overwhelming.

Marcus felt as if he existed not in reality but in an incredible dream that at any moment he would wake from. He had found himself feeling this more often as his emotions for this woman grew from the simple seed of affection to the large stalwart tree of love that now stood firmly planted in his heart, this feeling was one he tried to ignore, hide and deny.

This woman who lived alone did not need more attention from men, nor did she need the one she had entrusted into her home causing her discomfort he mentally sighed, once again Marcus closed his feelings behind the iron gates of denial before proceeding towards the simple farm table that now stood with a bowl of bread and freshly churned butter.

The house was warm as a fire illuminated the room as the single source of light, the worn iron pot hung suspended over the old stone hearth wearing the rising flames like a warm blanket in winter, the smell of garlic and onion clung to the air, a tease of the meal to come.

The petite woman stood stooping over the worn cauldron, her face a mask of fierce concentration as she slowly and deliberately stirred the fragrant concoction.

Marcus set about putting plates and utensils out for the meal and once she indicated that the pot was done, he helped by ladling it into a large serving bowl, placing it with the rest of the morning feast as he did every morning, he stood by the table, Orah joining him a moment later, Marcus waited until she took her seat before settling in himself

The two in companionable silence, Orah busying herself serving simple egg and vegetable dish.

He could not help but stare at this woman, this incredible woman who was the heart and strength of the farm.

Marcus had spent the last few months struggling with his feelings, his mind roiling as the factions within him warred, the urge to finally tell Orah how he felt exceeding his minds ability to suppress it, he felt the moment the wall keeping his emotions at bay began to crack, the damn breaking, only the fear of what that would do to their relationship choked off the words off leaving them trapped in his throat, the weight of them nearly causing him to suffocate.

Orah looked at him annoyed, the line of her brow arching as once again he moved to speak and as before stopped, instead staring at her dumbfounded, his mouth opening and closing like a fish out of water, finally, defeated he dropped his eyes looking down into the food that had begun to get cold in front of him.

“Today, move your things into my room” she finally said and then continued eating as if nothing had happened as if she had not put into words everything that Marcus had been hoping for, since he had first laid eyes on her. So many thoughts and emotions battled in his head. Entire speech’s flitted through his conscious mind in a second and finally opening his mind to unleash this torrent of emotion, pulling the only words he could from the cacophony of oration filling his brain, he said “What?” the idiotic expression complimenting the word.

Orah shook her head giving him another annoyed look, but her face quickly softened turning more sympathetic as she watched Marcus struggling.

“I know, I feel the same as you have for the past few months, but if I waited for you to make the first move I would be long dead and you would be speaking to my grave, so for Aurtus sake, please move into the house, live with me like I have desired you to for over a month, I love you Marcus and you love me anything else required is simply ceremony which I will be happy to stand in front of the Messenger and announce my intention to spend the rest of my life with you” she finished a smile spreading across her face.

Marcus shot out of his chair laughing with joy as he plucked her from the seat and swung the love of his life around, she squealed like a little girl throwing her arms around him there lips touching for the first time as he kissed the last pair of lips he ever wanted to touch.

Later that morning as they lay in bed, sweat still glistening on her alabaster skin as he ran gentle kisses along her hip as she lay on her side, facing him, the taste of her reigniting his passions, their feelings consummated on the simple wooden bed.

Marcus lazily ran his hands over the soft flesh of her lower back. The two had sealed their love becoming a couple in the primal way humans did.

“I love you Orah” he said speaking the words for the first time and he watched the way her face lit up as he uttered them. Sitting up she turned towards him as her hand rose to stroke his face her gentle fingertips sending electric shocks through his skin “I know Marcoos, I love you too” she answered, he smiled at her continued mispronunciation of his name and moved close to Orah, gathering her up in his arms he curled around her, bringing her in to snuggle up against him, the two lying there basking in the afterglow until finally they fell asleep in each other’s arms.

The chores and plans for the day forgotten as he reveled in their closeness, doing their best to keep reality at bay.

As the sun rose to mid-day and the reality of the farm bit at his mind he finally, reluctantly got up, gently removing himself from her bed as he tried to let her to sleep.

Marcus got dressed doing his best to leave the small cabin quietly, with a happy sigh he pulled his jacket closed against the cold air of the winter day and went around feeding the now hungry and annoyed animals that had been neglected all morning.

He refilled the woodpile near the hearth from the chord of wood stacked behind the cabin. He picked the final bounty of winter vegetables from the small garden in the back of the cabin.

He felt a tinge of sadness knowing this would be the last of the fresh produce until spring, they would survive off of canned goods, grain and smoked meat until the next year.

Carrying the basket of vegetables he entered the house, gently placing it on the table near the kitchen so that Orah could work her magic extending the life of the food by canning and making pottage, the stew being wasn’t his first choice for a meal, but in winter you ate what you had.

Marcus walked back into the bedroom to find Orah awake and staring back at him, her eyes as bright as her smile, He felt the last of the cold that clung to his skin melt away with the heat that spread through his body at the sight of that lovely smile.

“Hey, I need to run to town. Want to join me?” he asked her and leaning over, gently ran his hands lovingly through her blonde locks, Orah leaned her head back enjoying the feeling as he brushed a few loose locks from her forehead.

“No my love, I have many things to do here, go to town but be back soon,” she said, leaning up to kiss him. Marcus left sometime later with a spring in his step and a song on his lips. After a good fifteen-minute deliberation he decided to make the trip on foot, his skills with the horse still not up to a level where he felt comfortable riding alone. Besides the walk would do him good he thought pulling the leather jacket tighter as the cold air bit into his exposed skin.

He walked along the old dirt farm road; the cold had frozen the wet ground causing it to crunch under his feet with each step.

He did his best to keep out of the deep ruts caused by the narrow wooden tires of carriages as they made their way towards the small town to trade or purchase supplies, from his pocket he produced a small silver coin called a silverling, it had the bust of the emperor on one side and a dragon on the other, showing the relationship between the ruling family and the mages, closing his eyes Marcus took a breath, clearing his thoughts.

Clearing his mind, he reached out feeling the resistance of the coin, unlike the branch there was no thrumming of life, the metal was dead but still he could feel its mass, like a resistance against his conscious thoughts.

Recalling the instructions in the small worn book he lightly pushed at the small coin feeling it grow lighter in his hand as he pushed on the underside of the small piece of precious metal, opening his eyes he watched it hover an inch above his palm and smiled.

He kept the coin in his mind as he continued to walk, a small flock of the flying snakes took off from a tree and soared overhead. He had talked to Orah more than once about the various animal she had encountered. The snakes were called Surioun and from the way she had discussed it, it appeared to be a run of the mill forest creature, her description was no different than if she had been talking about a raccoon or a squirrel, but still Marcus stared after the creatures with amazement until they disappeared out of view over the next line of trees.

He continued to let his mind wander, the parts that weren’t concentrating on the coin anyway and thought about the life he had left behind.

The computers, internet, cars and planes a; relegated to thoughts of fancy, his existence now stripped down to the basics, his only concern had to do with ensuring that he harvested enough food to survive instead of who was flaming who on Facebook this week.

He felt the coin grow heavy against his mind, the longer he floated it, the more concentration he needed in order to keep it floating. It was something the book described, the exercise that he was currently doing allowed him to strengthen his connection with the power, allowing him to reinforce his ability to channel it.

According to the book, those with the gift had the ability to tap into the crystals and harness the power directing it to their will. It still sounded crazy the more he talked about it, but then again, he had just watched a flock of flying snakes soar overhead while he levitated a coin in his hand, a small smile spreading over his face at the sheer lunacy of it.

He spent the rest of the journey admiring the woods and other small farms along the road.

After a time his thoughts went back to ARC, the project that had been created to save mankind, it was obvious something catastrophic had happened but then humans were still here, so in some form the project had succeeded, he just wished he had a better grasp of the past.

The smile fell off his face as he once again reflected on the wars and warlords that had come, everyone who shared his knowledge of earth, his earth was now long dead, the lessons they would have brought with them seemed to either have fallen on deaf ears or not been passed at all. With an effort he pushed those thoughts away, instead thinking of Orah’s smile replaying the mornings adventures, the smile quickly returning.

Marcus spent time reflecting once again on the creeping isolation he felt when comparing this world to the one he had known all his life, his world where people spent their lives going from one screen to the next, phones and computers and email and texts were the fabric that bound people, however here the speed of life was slower, simpler, you had time to think, to contemplate your life, existence was narrowed to surviving and you took the happy moments where you could find them he mused.

It took Marcus longer than usual, his pace slowing as his mind worked through the thoughts of life in this new world, cresting the now-familiar final hill, the view of the large wall came into sight, the silhouette of the small town of Powrie appearing before him.

As Marcus approached, he could just make out the shadow of the Lord Seer’s keep like a specter upon the hill against the still clinging fog,

Orah had explained a bit about the man who was tasked with rule over the area by the Emperor himself.

From what he had heard Seer Galen was not a man who valued his workers, nor would she describe him as benevolent, putting the keep out of his mind he approached the gate and smiled, nodding a greeting as the guards waved him through.

Entering the city he spied a few people strolling the main market street, some in the simple cotton of farmworkers and others wearing their Sunday best just having come from the keep, he smiled as he watched them shopping or visiting with friends, with no paper or internet people went to town to find out the latest gossip or to just get away from the daily routine of the farm, it was an adventure, an event and one that they looked forward to he thought walking towards the large stone keep.

Marcus smiled as he spotted Messenger Veric standing outside the stone building, resplendent in the simple brown corded robes of his office, like a proud doting parent he kept a watchful eye on his flock as they moved about the town.

“Hello, my friend. I apologize for my tardiness” Marcus said walking over towards the keep. Veric looked his friend over and must have seen something in his face because his own lit up and a wide smile spread over his features “She said yes” the messenger breathed excitedly.

Marcus regarded his friend for a moment was it that obvious he thought and then decided it probably was, he had been walking on air since leaving the farm, it would not be a far stretch that it showed all over his face.

“She did” he answered and Veric clapped him on the back as he led him into the old Keep.

“This is cause for celebration the man said, his thin build a contrast to the booming voice that erupted with a cheer for his friend as he led him into to his private chambers.

Marcus smiled shyly walking over and sitting down at the simple wooden table, Veric closing the door, quickly moved to the simple kitchenette, listened to the rustling as the Messenger rummaged around in a cabinet was comforting to the younger man, after a few minutes producing a dusty leather skin Veric gently removed the cap smelling at the liquid inside appreciatively before bringing it over to the table, stopping only long enough to grab two glasses from the cabinet.

“This my friend is a cause for celebration” he exclaimed excitedly. Marcus took the glass raising it in a toast and then downing the concoction. The drink burned a fiery trail down his throat causing him to gasp and cough.

Veric laughed shaking his head “I know its flavor has a lot to be desired, but it does get the job done my friend” he finished amicably pouring Marcus another glass of the amber liquid.

They sat and drank talking for almost two hours, Veric telling stories of some of the townsfolk and the antics they would get into.

Marcus had not laughed so hard in his life. Smiling he had said his goodbyes to the old Messenger, and he could truly call Veric that.

The two had formed a close bond since he had first visited the Keep though Marcus was not religious nor did he visit the church often. Every time he came to town, he would always make time to sit down with Veric.

As he was about to leave a young man came into the keep and handed the Messenger a folded and sealed letter. Veric looked confused as he nodded and broke the seal of the church that stood upon the wax seal.

He quickly read it and Marcus watched as the man’s normally jovial face fell. “What is it my friend?” he asked, concerned, he had never seen the older man look so worried.

Veric gently closed the letter and was quiet for a moment. Looking at his friend, he finally spoke, his words sending a chill down Marcus’s spine.

“Let Orah know that dark times are coming. Marcus, the emperor is dead, and the church is taking up a collection for the Outcasts so we can try to move them to Dever or Lusor.

The Empress has no love for the children of the crystal, and I fear what she might do.” He avoided Marcus’ eyes as he finished that last statement.

He shivered a little remembering a story from his own past in which whole people were slaughtered in the name of purity.

“What is an outcast?” Marcus asked not having heard the term, Veric looking surprised “They don’t have them where you’re from, the children of the crystal, the ones who have been changed by generations of living in proximity to so many of them?” the Messenger asked.

With a sigh he shook his head and leaned against the solid oak door frame “They are a sad people Marcus, over the generations they have been transformed either by ingestion of the crystal dust from mining or just living too close to them, we really do not know, the church at one time called them heathens and the children of Mephis, long before the Mages became our target, but since then we have strived to ensure they receive a better life, they are a people who have lived hard and have earned the honor and respect of all, they are the miners of the crystal, the reason we have the technology we do, but it had come at a cost” he finished and Marcus noticed he skipped over the part of what the church had done, but the man’s guilt was evident whatever had happened had formed the church’s need to make amends and that was more than a lot of those who were responsible for atrocities did he thought.

“How come I have never seen them or heard them spoken of?” he asked. Pretty sure if odd people were walking around anywhere someone would talk about it, though he had not spent much time in town he had spent enough where something like that would have made its way to him. The messenger shook his head in sadness.

“They are not allowed to leave the Barrens, most still consider them evil or tied to evil and to speak of them would bring bad omens, so they tend to avoid the subject,” he finished looking out the window over the small town.

“They are good people Marcus, just simple, they ride the line between life and death survival there only reward” he finished as if justifying their actions. Marcus just nodded following the old man’s gaze.

After a few moments, he said his goodbyes and promised to come back soon.

Leaving the keep he made his way down the center of the small village finally coming to the shop of the Crystal Smith, part of him yearned to talk to the old shop keeper, to find out more about the Mages and the magic, but still he held back, something about the way Mages were treated gave him pause.

What would happen should they find out about him, what would become of Orah, the woman who harbored an unregistered mage he wondered, Marcus stared at the front of the building trying to decide if today he would reveal himself to the shopkeeper, he had questions and this man might have the answers, he was after all a mage like himself Marcus admitted.

Since moving into Orah’s Marcus’s ability to sense the crystals had grown, his power to control had also grown with the help of the book.

He had heard the stories of the early ARC members, his people and the powers they had. Marcus worried that sooner or later he would end up losing control and hurting not only himself but Orah or perhaps others, he was hesitant to talk to the man, but he needed more information and possibly more training.

How could he ask the questions he needed to without arousing the suspicion of the man, the last thing he needed was to have this Mage find out who or what he was, he might turn him in to the order, Marcus would not leave Orah or allow others to remove him from her, he would die before he aloud anyone to come between them. With a deep breath he entered the small shop.

It was much the same as he remembered, the small area cluttered with shelf upon shelf of crystals, resin dust and devices. He slowly perused the closest shelf as he made his way towards the counter where the portly mage stood with a smile on his face as he expectantly awaited another potential sale.

“Aaah, young master Marcoos, I remember you, but you have not visited my store in many months, I was starting to take it personally” the big man said with mock sadness causing Marcus to smile as he sidled up to the counter can’t anyone fucking say my name right he thought. “I have been busy my friend, but I am here now” he answered returning the other man’s smile.

“Have you finished the book?” the shop keeper asked, and Marcus nodded cautiously. He thought he sensed a knowing smile from the man but didn’t rise to the bait “It was good information, though not practical for someone without powers” he stated to the shop keeper nonchalantly, the man nodded and did not pursue it further.

Finally, after a short uncomfortable silence the older man spoke “How may I help you today?” Marcus began looking over some of the crystals mostly to avoid eye contact.

“There are a few things I am interested in looking at, but most of all, I have a few questions as I am unfamiliar with the spells and machines and even the crystals, where I come from these are not known” he said keeping to his traveler story.

The man looked shocked, as if that were not even possible. “What questions may I answer” he asked after recovering, Marcus surprised he never even asked him about where he was from, usually that was the first question he got.

He nodded at the portly mage, “I have heard that the first to return.” he blanched before quickly correcting himself “be brought down from the gods had incredible powers, is that true?” he finished, and the Shop Keeper nodded gravely.

“It is, all of us are descended from those who came first, however the gift has lost a lot of its potency since the first, according to the accounts they had far more power at their fingertips then even the strongest mage today, I am afraid, over the centuries fewer and fewer babies have been born with the gift, I fear that one day the Magi will see its end in the not too distant future” he answered his voice rife with sadness.

“I know there was a time when the church, the mage and the crown were at war and that is the reason your face is marked, but I also notice that most people seem to resent you or are scared, but I am not sure why?” he asked. Marcus had seen people avoid the mages had heard the stories of them taking babies or casting spells on people.

There was a lot of fear shown towards the magi, but they seem to be impervious to it, never acknowledging it and always friendly and helpful.

The Shopkeeper nodded “Aye, that there is, but they also need us and know it. People fear the unknown and we are that unknown, they tell stories and they avoid us until such time as they need healing or a cooking appliance’s for their home or a spell for their wife or horse, but that is our existence, we understand it and don’t hold it against the people” he finished, Marcus nodded but didn’t agree with the statement, people were closed minded and opinionated even in his time, but that didn’t mean people should stand for it or give them a pass.

There would always be animosity from those ignorant people who would fear what they could not understand, but the keeper was right, they needed the mages, so they were safe, existing somewhere between that which is tolerated and feared he thought.

“What happens when you discover someone with power?” he asked getting right to the real question that had been on his mind. The man looked Marcus over, regarding him silently as if trying to decide how to answer the question.

“Why do you ask?” he said but his eyes told him knew already, and Marcus’s blood went cold, how was it possible that this man knew so surely that Marcus himself was a mage he wondered.

“No reason, it was a stupid question, I need to go” Marcus blurted, suddenly wanting very much to leave, practically running out of the store before the shopkeeper could protest.

Once he had closed the door of the shop, he leaned against it for a moment, chiding himself for being so stupid.

Walking across the courtyard of the small town, the hum of crystals still resonated in his mind as the large collection stood like a beacon to his mind, to his relief the shop keeper had not followed him.

With a sigh Marcus walked towards the entrance gate just as a shadow fell across his face, stopping in his tracks he looked up and gawked despite this not being the first time he had seen it.

The large, sailing ship was much closer than the last one he had witnessed and event was surreal as the wooden sailing vessel came to a stop, floating above the small town. Marcus watched as four people launched themselves over the side of the wooden balcony of the airship and rapidly descending along ropes that fell to the ground.

As they approached, the four people flipped landing gently on their feet, the ships mates guided the vessel down, the large ship creaking as it slowed, hovering just above the earth as the airman tied it to a large iron horn that Marcus had not noticed before.

“It’s quite a sight isn’t it?” came a voice from behind Marcus. He turned to find a stocky man with an earnest smile spread across his face. The man wore a simple blue cotton jumpsuit, stepping up he extended his hand.

“Hornsby, I’m Powrie’s dockmaster and owner of the general store” he stated, and Marcus absently took his hand.

“Dock Master?” he asked almost detached as his eyes once again went to the large ship hovering, actually hovering his mind repeated trying to wrap his mind around it.

“I didn’t know the town had a dock master, much less needed one” he said his eyes roving over the ship as the sails lowered and were stowed, he could hear the shouted orders across the deck, but couldn’t make out the words, At this distance he could make out the detail of the gold filigree that adorned the side and the gold figure of a woman that hung from the bow, if he didn’t know better he would think it had sailed right out of the 1800’s. He heard the man chuckle “We usually don’t, we get very few airships out this way, they are more common in the larger cities, but with the Seer we sometimes get one or two a year, being dockmaster is an easy job and pays a little stipend to help ends meet” the man said affably.

“How does it move through the air” Marcus called, Again, the man chuckled “Crystals, they use crystals to move the ship, I don’t know exactly how it works but I bet if you ask a mage, they could tell you” he said.

“Well, I have a job to do, you might want to move, when the excursion vessel comes down, you don’t want to be in the way” he said and Marcus looked at him and then the ship again, realizing he was standing directly below it. “My apologies” he said and walked a little way towards the exit.

Once he thought he was far enough to be safe he turned in time to see a small flat-bottomed boat with two rows of crystals set into the underside, glowing as the small boat gently floated to the ground. Inside were two well-dressed men who looked as if they too were some kind of royalty.

Marcus decided it was better not to stick around and be noticed. He made his way back to the farm, to his life and woman he loved. The sun was coming on dusk as he finally reached the small farm the first thing, he noticed was the horses out front and the two men standing on the porch, as Marcus drew closer he sensed something wasn’t right from where he was the look on Orah’s face was almost terror.

Quickening his pace, he entered the yard coming to stand at the base of the porch.

As soon as Orah spotted him she bolted into his arms leaving the two men looking annoyed at Marcus. “Can I help you” Marcus asked an edge of hostility in his words as he sensed the fear and felt Orah trembling under his touch.

The two did not miss it either. The one on the right, taller than his friend and also outweighing Marcus by a good fifty pounds laid his hand on the butt of a pistol, caressing it as he eyed the newcomer.

Marcus noticed the brown leather outfit they both wore, almost like a uniform he thought an emblem of the raven pinned just above the breast. The same as the guards who stood sentry in the village, he thought they both wore the Mark of Galen Bor.

Marcus pushed Orah behind him leaving himself between her and the two men now leering at her. Carefully he assessed the two men, figuring out quickly that he was severely under-armed for the encounter, but as the anger rose in his chest so did something else as power thrummed through his body, closing his eyes he forced it down, now was not the time to demonstrate those abilities he thought.

The overweight one, Marcus mentally named him pudgy for obvious reasons, gave him pause, it was something in his eyes he thought, they looked almost dead, devoid of any emotion, chills ran down his spine as the man produced two more pistols from behind his back and held them loosely pointed in Marcus’s direction.

As if that weren’t enough, his friend laid a hand to rest on the Bastard sword that hung in a scabbard on his belt. The Swordsman, a much taller and thinner than his gun toting friend had a pinched face, giving him a look like he had pulled a muscle permanently.

Marcus named him Weasel, as his facial features strongly resembled one, Weasel kept looking back to pudgy as if waiting for a signal. Okay. So, we know who is in charge, Marcus thought.

The man also carried a very long knife that slung cocked forward on his hip for easier unsheathing. Pudgy’s little beady blue eyes roved over Orah as he took a step forward his cheeks and double chin spreading into a smile, but not one Marcus would call friendly.

Weasel mimicked the leering smile, stepping towards the two as well. Marcus held his ground, tensing as the two men stopped within kicking distance of the him.

Marcus didn’t know what he had walked into, but he knew the look on the two men’s faces, the lurid smiles and excited beady eyes, he shivered at the thought of what would have happened had he not shown up, the two men nodding and moving again.

Marcus didn’t miss the way the man pulled to the right, thus if he had to shoot both of the men would have clear fields of fire on him, the unarmed civilian.

“Our business is not with you, friend, so move on,” the pudgy one stated his tone hostile, Marcus’s lack of a sword making the man bold he thought.

“If your business is about the farm, then it is with me. Either state your business, friend, or piss off,” Marcus said, taking a step forward. His expression caused the thin one to take an involuntary step back, bullies he thought don’t show fear.

Pudgy’s hands tightened on his pistols as he slowly pulled the hammers back, a metallic sound emitting from the guns, Marcus Tightened his hand on Orah’s, he did his best not to wince knowing that sound meant the wheel guns were now only a hair’s breadth away from spewing death.

Marcus pointedly looked down at the weapons then met Pudgy’s dull brown eyes. His eyes flashing anger as if daring the big man to pull the trigger, whatever the large man saw caused him a moment of pause, the pistols wavered a bit, but did not move away from Marcus. Trying to save face Pudgy did his best approximation of a companionable smile, his jowls shaking as he nodded his head, taking a different tact.

“Of course, of course, We are here to collect this year’s taxes, we are the collectors and our records indicate this farm owes fifty silverlings, however if you do not have it, then other arrangements can be made” he said licking his lips as he shot a lascivious glance behind him to Orah.

Heat welled up in Marcus as he understood the man’s meaning, and with every ounce of will he had, he unclenched his fists, taking a breath as the power in his chest began to heat, rising yet again along with his anger, he forced it down doing his best to calm himself despite the pictures of what these men would do to the woman he loved playing in his mind.

Marcus slowly reached into the small leather bag tied to his belt and pulling out a handful of silver pieces. He counted out fifty, most of what the farm had for money and handed it to the man.

“You can go now,” he said, trying to keep calm as every muscle in his body tensed wanting nothing more than to beat this man into the ground. The Weasel looked over at the small pile of coins, his look of disappointment evident.

“Morlin, you know I think we might just leave the money and take it in trade” his friend stated, as he finished his words the sword began to rise out of its scabbard as Weasel came to stand in an overhead guard position.

He had obviously set his sights on Orah and he wouldn’t be denied. His fat friend shot him a worried glance and then looked back at Marcus.

Everything slowed for a moment, the three men standing, eyeing one another.

Weasel made his move, Marcus watched with a detached fascination as the man’s hand moved and the sword came free of the scabbard. Once he understood the man’s intent Marcus was in motion, the power he had suppressed now surging forward, augmenting his reflexes and strength, training over-riding thought, with a quick step forward he came to stand before pudgy, slamming his foot on top of the other man’s, using the heal he heard bones crack, Pudgy’s eyes widened as he screamed in pain, turning Marcus grabbed one of the pistols as it fell from the fat man’s hand and spun, bringing the pistol to bear on Weasel.

His hand steady as the weapon now leveled at the gaunt man. But Weasel wouldn’t be denied, with an expert flourish of the blade he swung, Marcus dodged but not fast enough, his skill with the power still novice, felt the cold metal of the blades tip light along the side of his neck.

A trickle of something wet slid along the burning wound.

As the blade came to a stop, a blue flash of energy shattered the metal above the hilt, Weasel stood there stunned, his eyes wide as he stared in disbelief at was left of his sword.

“You have your money, you will leave, or I will be shipping you back to your master in little boxes” Marcus whispered, moving the gun to level on Weasel’s head, Weasel eyed the pistol and then rose his gaze to look into Marcus’s eyes whatever he saw, he didn’t like and Marcus saw the moment the man made the decision to back down, Weasel dropping the broken hilt, the dull thump punctuating defeat.

Pudgy had recovered, and Marcus shot the man a withering glare causing him to take an involuntary step back. These men were bullies and like most bullies when they sensed a fair fight, they barked and ran. “Leave before I change my mind” Marcus said, a moment later both men bolted for the road and quickly mounted their horses, turning to face Marcus both men shot him hostile stares.

“You have no idea what you have done, this disrespect will not stand dirt born, you have not heard the last of us” he said glaring at Marcus for a moment before they coaxed the horses out of the yard both setting off at a gallop towards town.

Marcus leaned over picking up the discarded pistol, he stood outside holding Orah in comfort but his dominant hand still pointing the pistol towards the road.

Once the adrenaline had expired and the power began to wane from his body, doubt set in, what had he done, he had been angry but know he wondered what repercussions would occur because of his need to slap those two for their insulting glares and words.

Orah pushed herself closer and Marcus dropped the weapon, wrapping her fully in his arms. “Are you okay?” he whispered gently, and with her head in the crook of his arm, she nodded.

He gently guided her back into the house as he listened to the fading hooves of the collector’s horses.
